title: The Contract Inside a Tool Definition

questions.question: A tool takes no parameters. Which inputSchema is the recommended way to declare that, so only an empty object is accepted?
options: A null value, left out entirely so no client validates the call at all
type object alone, which accepts any object, including one with properties
type object with additionalProperties false, accepting only empty objects
An empty schema with no type keyword, which accepts any JSON value at all
questions.explanation: The recommended no-parameter form is type object with additionalProperties false, which explicitly accepts only an empty object; inputSchema must never be null.

questions.question: A tool's inputSchema has no $schema field at all. Which dialect governs how a client validates arguments against it in 2026-07-28?
options: Draft-07, kept as the fallback default for compatibility with older servers
Whichever dialect the connecting client's own SDK happens to be built against
OpenAPI 3.1's schema object, since MCP tool schemas reuse its object model
JSON Schema 2020-12, the default dialect a schema uses when $schema is absent
questions.explanation: When a schema omits $schema, MCP defaults it to JSON Schema 2020-12; a schema may declare a different dialect explicitly, but 2020-12 is always the fallback.

questions.question: A tool declares an outputSchema and a call to it succeeds. What should the result contain, per the 2026-07-28 tools specification?
options: structuredContent conforming to outputSchema, plus the same data serialized as text
Only structuredContent, since a schema-conformant value makes any text redundant
A resource_link pointing at a URI where the structured value can be fetched later
Only a text content block, because structuredContent belongs to resources, not tools
questions.explanation: A result should carry structuredContent that conforms to outputSchema, and for backward compatibility it should also serialize that same value into a TextContent block.

questions.question: A tools/call argument fails the tool's inputSchema, for instance a required field is missing. What does a conformant 2026-07-28 server return?
options: A normal result with isError set to false, since the server produced a response
A normal result with isError set to true and content explaining what to fix
A JSON-RPC error, code -32602, because invalid arguments are a protocol-level fault
A JSON-RPC error, code -32601, because the requested method could not be located
questions.explanation: SEP-1303 moved input validation failures into tool execution errors: a normal result with isError true and an explanation the model can read and correct on its next call.

questions.question: A tool's inputSchema has a $ref that resolves to https://schemas.example.com/common.json. What should a conformant implementation do with that reference by default?
options: Reject the whole tool definition outright, since inputSchema may never contain a ref
Fetch the URL the first time it validates the schema, then cache the response
Refuse to dereference it automatically, since network refs need an explicit opt-in
Treat the referenced property as unconstrained and accept whatever value arrives there
questions.explanation: Implementations must not automatically dereference a $ref that resolves to a network URI; fetching one is opt-in only, disabled by default, and guarded by an allowlist when offered.

questions.question: Which of these candidate tool names satisfies the naming rules a conformant 2026-07-28 server should follow?
options: A 200 character name built by concatenating a full sentence about the tool
"get user", separating the two words in the name with a plain space
get/user@2026, mixing a forward slash with an at sign in one name
admin.tools.list, built only from letters and dots and no spaces at all
questions.explanation: Tool names should stay within 1 to 128 characters of letters, digits, underscore, hyphen, and dot; spaces, an at sign, and a slash all fall outside that allowed character set.
